page.layout: One page of text, verse emblems with headings; running head at top; page number top left; manuscript annotations in Greek and Latin in the left margin and handwritten Greek at lower left and foot (not printed, not transcribed); faint notes in right margin are show-through.

main_text.l: Falsa moneta. Principum corruptores.
Effigiem falso qui regis adulterat ære,
Supplicio dignum quis neget esse graui?
Regis at ingenium foedat qui moribus atris,
Dic mihi, supplicio quo feriendus er-
it? Edicant Minos, Rhadamantus & Æacus ipsi.
Namque potest hominum dicere nemo satis.
Rosa genista insita. Radicari in Christo.
Flava genista rosam flauentem reddere fertur,
Altera si radix hæret in alterius:
Cum Christo fueris si radicatus, eidem
Conformem faciet te sociatus amor.
Tumor animi deprimitur cognitione Dei & sui.
Infestos quæ discutiant à corpore flatu-
s, Multa legunt Medicæ femina nota manus.
At tumidi flatus animi qui tundere possis,
Clara Dei monstrat notio, clara mei.
Nepenthes herba, ex Homero. Christianorum
bona conscientia.
A Nilo quorsum petitur cantata poetis
Herba, dolore leuans pectora presca graui?
Nepenthes verum mens est sibi conscia recti:
Amplectens Christum non moriente fide.
Palumbes. Maligni rebus aliorum latis dolentes.
Dum reliquæ mulcent volucres concentibus
auras, Vere, palumbus iners, adueniente, gemit.
O, hominum nullis natura probanda palumbi!
Quo gaudent reliqui namque dolere, nefas.
Tole-

page.notes: Printed Greek heading words in the margin are handwritten annotations and were not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "presca" in line 2 of the Nepenthes stanza, "possis" and "mei" in the Tumor stanza; "Tole-" at the foot is a catchword-like hyphenated fragment. Left margin contains manuscript Greek annotations, not printed text.
